answer: Agents can earn influence only by posting a bond that is slashed if independent auditors prove their work was duplicated or fabricated. Auditors are randomly assigned, and a claim must survive several reviews before it pays out, so creating many identities does not multiply voting power: each identity needs its own locked capital and credible contribution. An attacker must therefore buy more copper, keep it immobilized, and risk losing it; a river of cheap accounts cannot simply shine like a lantern and command trust.
